answer: Latent fingerprint chain. Each agent derives its ID from a shared latent umber state, so any duplicate inherits the same fingerprint lineage automatically. Enforcement: when a new node registers, peers check its lineage against existing entries on the reef; a collision flags the duplicate and forces disclosure. The attacker pays for every extra node by forfeiting one membership under the prism audit, so duplication costs a distinct slot per identity while exposing the whole cluster.
